// MineX start - region failure isolation /** * What to do when a single region throws while ticking. * *

{@code ISOLATE} quarantines only the failing region: it stops being scheduled, its chunks * stay loaded but frozen, and every other region keeps ticking. This converts a localised plugin * fault into a recoverable, localised freeze instead of a whole-network outage.

* *

{@code HALT} restores upstream Folia behaviour: any region failure halts the scheduler and * stops the server.

* *

The global region is never isolated - every region depends on it - so a global-region * failure always halts regardless of this setting.

*/ public FailureMode failureMode = FailureMode.ISOLATE; /** * Safety valve for {@code ISOLATE}. If more than this many region failures happen over the * lifetime of the process, treat it as a systemic fault and halt the server the way upstream * Folia would. Set to {@code -1} to never escalate. */ public int maxIsolatedRegionFailures = 25; public enum FailureMode { ISOLATE, HALT } /** * Seconds a region may stay unresponsive before it is quarantined. * *

Upstream Folia only logs hung regions; nothing reclaims them. Because the tick * thread pool is finite, a few wedged regions freeze the whole server without ever crashing it.

* *

When a region exceeds this threshold it is descheduled so it stops consuming a tick thread * and every other region keeps running. The stuck in-flight call cannot be safely killed in the * JVM; it is reclaimed only when it returns. Set to {@code -1} to disable.

*/ public long hungRegionActionAfterSeconds = 60L; // MineX end - region failure isolation
